NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
Proposed mitigation: Implement a "High-Temperature Scour Pulse" procedure by periodically raising the oxidizer wall temperature setpoint above the standard operating point to thermally desorb and volatilize accumulating TiO2 species, while simultaneously modulating the O2:TiCl4 feed ratio to maintain stoichiometric excess oxygen.
Mechanism: By transiently increasing the wall temperature $T_w$, the desorption rate constant $k_{des}$ increases exponentially (Arrhenius behavior), and the equilibrium partial pressure of TiCl4/TiO species increases, shifting the reaction equilibrium away from solid deposition and toward the gas phase. Simultaneously, a transient increase in the O2:TiCl4 ratio ensures that any volatilized Ti species are rapidly oxidized to volatile TiCl4 in the bulk flow, preventing re-nucleation at cooler wall sections. Furthermore, maintaining an excess P_O2 (higher O2:TiCl4 ratio) shifts the equilibrium constant for the formation of volatile TiCl4 over solid TiO2, reducing the thermodynamic driving force for R_dep.
